prompt: A loading ramp is $15$ ft long and rises at an angle of $20^\circ$ to the ground. How high is the top of the ramp above the ground, in feet, rounded to the nearest tenth?
hint: The ramp itself is the hypotenuse; the height is opposite the $20^\circ$ angle.

hints.text: The ramp itself is the hypotenuse; the height is opposite the $20^\circ$ angle.

explanation: Label the triangle: hypotenuse $= 15$ (the ramp), unknown height opposite the $20^\circ$ angle.
Opposite over hypotenuse is sine, so $\sin 20^\circ = \frac{h}{15}$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Does the size make sense?
steps: A shallow $20^\circ$ climb should gain only a little height over $15$ ft of travel.
About $5$ ft of rise for $15$ ft of ramp feels right; an answer like $14$ ft would mean a nearly vertical ramp.
